text: You can see Africa from Europe. It's 14 kilometers away. So why can't you drive there?
That's shorter than Manhattan. The channel tunnel is 50 kilometers. So 14 should be easy.
Right?
Here's the catch. The problem isn't the distance. It's the depth. Up to 900 meters.
Drop in the Burj Khalifa and it vanishes. Add fierce currents,
plates, colliding plates, and one of the world's busiest chipping lanes.
So how do you join two continents?
Rewind to 1928.
A German architect, Hermann Zurgl, had a plan.
Damn the strait and drain the Mediterranean by up to 200 meters.
New land, about the size of France.
Nobody asked the fish.
It never happened.
In 1979, Spain and Morocco agreed to link up.
Let's build it! Deal! When do we start?
Right after...one more study.
47 years later, one study came back different.
It's possible. A rail tunnel, 475 meters below the sea,
four times deeper than the channel tunnel,
spaying to Morocco in 30 minutes.
Ready by 2035? Maybe 2040, too late for the 2030 World Cup. Or just wait, Africa creeps
toward Europe millimeters a year, give it millions of years, and the gap should close
for free. Until then, don't worry.
